summary: Define a reusable timing and pose grammar whose selected, active, waiting, complete and error states remain distinguishable at hold frames, interruption points and reduced motion.
objective: Motion gives unlike objects a shared character without making state depend on continuous movement or one transition finishing.
applies_when: Animation communicates application or simulation state as well as atmosphere.
Characters, mechanisms and interface-linked objects need a shared motion character.
intent_signals: motion style that keeps state readable
shared timing language across character and machine
example_prompts: Give a courier and a parcel sorter the same quick-anticipate, firm-settle motion language while selected, jammed and complete states remain readable when paused.
negative_signals: Encoding loading or error only through looping motion.
Assuming every transition reaches its authored end pose.
not_for: A clip-authoring tutorial or animation retargeting contract.
A claim that one easing curve is universally legible.

principles: Separate state pose from transition flavor. Every meaningful state gets a stable geometry, material, label or pattern cue; anticipation, overshoot and cadence decorate the route between states.
Define entry, hold, exit and interruption behavior for each motion family. Preserve continuity from the sampled current pose and make priorities explicit when state changes overlap.
Provide a reduced-motion interpretation that preserves state and task completion while shortening, replacing or removing non-essential travel.
implementation: In Blender, author representative holds and transitions for two unlike objects, such as a character and sorting gate. Keep named state holds distinct from decorative loops and retain source curves for revision.

Export supported transform, skeletal or morph tracks as glTF animation. List unsupported constraints, drivers and procedural timing as baked animation or runtime-owned logic; transport does not define application state priority.

In Three.js, map application state to stable visual cues, choose clips or procedural transitions, and sample the current result before interruption. Query the user motion preference and select a bounded reduced-motion variant without removing status or control feedback.
observable_checks: Pause at each hold and at a mid-transition sample: selected, waiting, complete and error remain distinguishable through a non-motion cue.
Interrupt entry with exit and a decorative loop with an error state: no snap to an unrelated authored start and the higher-priority state wins.
Exercise the reduced-motion path: non-essential travel is minimized while state change, action completion and focus/selection feedback remain perceivable.

creative_affordances: Choose elastic, stepped, mechanical, weighty or restrained transitions per brief while keeping the same state/transition separation.
Allow distinct subjects to express the grammar through different joints, deformations or material pulses.
known_limits: A detected preference is an input to the authored runtime policy; it does not prescribe one universal replacement animation.
No motion preference, clip interruption or state legibility test was run.

claims.statement: Media Queries Level 5 defines prefers-reduced-motion as a discrete media feature with no-preference and reduce values for detecting a user request that the system minimize non-essential motion.
claims.scope: CSSWG Editor’s Draft read 2026-09-08; the application still owns which motion is essential and how state information is preserved.
